stages.title: FEDERALISM: AUTONOMY WITHIN A UNION OF STATES

groups.heading: DEFINITION
items: Constitution divides authority between Union and States.
Each operates directly in assigned fields.
Independent courts police the boundary.

groups.heading: INDIAN FORMATION
items: Article 1 says Union of States.
The Union is not a secession-permitting compact.
Holding-together design gives the Union greater strength.

groups.heading: FEDERAL FEATURES
items: Dual polity, written supreme Constitution and divided powers.
Rigidity for federal provisions.
Bicameral representation and independent judiciary.

stages.answer_line: Federal government constitutionally divides public power between a general government and regional governments so that each operates directly on citizens within an assigned sphere.

stages.title: UNION BIAS WITHOUT UNITARY ABSORPTION

groups.heading: CENTRALISING DESIGN
items: Broad Union fields and residuary power.
Exceptional Parliament access to State subjects.
Emergency, Governors and All-India Services.

groups.heading: INTEGRATING INSTITUTIONS
items: Single citizenship and integrated judiciary.
Election and audit architecture.
Flexible State reorganisation.

groups.heading: FEDERAL CHECKS
items: State List and elected State governments.
Rajya Sabha, ratification and judicial review.
Finance and intergovernmental bargaining; federalism as Basic Structure.

stages.answer_line: India's centralising features remain constitutional and reviewable, so they modify rather than extinguish federalism.

stages.title: LEGISLATIVE DISTRIBUTION AND CONFLICT DOCTRINES

groups.heading: LIST ARCHITECTURE
items: Article 245 controls territorial reach.
Article 246 orders Union, Concurrent and State fields.
Standard exam counts: 100, 61 and 52.

groups.heading: SPECIAL POWERS
items: Article 246A creates GST competence.
Article 248 and Union List Entry 97 vest residuary power in Parliament.
Article 254 addresses Concurrent repugnancy.

groups.heading: INTERPRETIVE CONTROL
items: Pith and substance identifies true nature.
Territorial nexus requires real connection.
Harmonious construction preserves fields; repugnancy resolves final conflict.

stages.answer_line: Article 248 and Union List Entry 97 place residuary legislative power with Parliament, including residuary taxation subject to later GST design.

stages.title: PARLIAMENT ON THE STATE LIST: EXCEPTION ROUTES

groups.heading: NATIONAL TRIGGERS
items: Article 249: Rajya Sabha national-interest resolution.
Article 250: National Emergency.
Article 253: treaty implementation.

groups.heading: STATE / TERRITORIAL TRIGGERS
items: Article 252: two or more States request Parliament.
Other States may adopt later; Parliament amends or repeals.
Article 246(4): non-State territories.

groups.heading: CRISIS TRIGGER / LIMIT
items: Article 356 enables Parliament for the affected State.
Each route has a distinct trigger and duration.
Exceptional access does not permanently erase List II.

stages.answer_line: Article 253 is powerful but remains subject to constitutional rights, judicial review and the actual treaty-implementation nexus.

stages.title: FEDERALISM AS BASIC STRUCTURE AND CASE CONTROL

groups.heading: IDENTITY
items: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) places federal character in the identity framework.
Union strength cannot erase State constitutional status.
Federalism limits constitutional amendment and power use.

groups.heading: ARTICLE 356
items: S.R. Bommai (1994) constrains partisan central intervention.
Disputed majority ordinarily goes to the floor.
Presidential action remains judicially reviewable.

groups.heading: GST FEDERALISM
items: Mohit Minerals (2022) treats GST Council recommendations as recommendatory.
Consultation and pooled sovereignty matter.
Union and State legislative autonomy remain constitutionally relevant.

stages.answer_line: The basic-structure cases transformed federalism from a descriptive feature into an enforceable limit on Union power, especially against partisan displacement of State governments.

stages.title: COOPERATION, COMPETITION, BARGAINING AND ASYMMETRY

groups.heading: OPERATING MODES
items: Cooperation coordinates interdependence.
Competition spreads innovation but may widen capacity gaps.
Bargaining accommodates interests; confrontation channels disputes.

groups.heading: SHARED RULE
items: Rajya Sabha, Inter-State Council and Zonal Councils.
GST Council, Finance Commission and courts.
All-India Services and dispute mechanisms.

groups.heading: ASYMMETRY / DEPTH
items: Special arrangements need constitutional source and purpose.
Local government deepens participation.
Local bodies are not a co-equal third sovereign tier.

stages.answer_line: The health test is whether institutions convert confrontation into reasons, negotiation, adjudication and electoral accountability.

stages.title: FISCAL FEDERALISM: CAPACITY, EQUALISATION AND GST

groups.heading: REVENUE / EXPENDITURE GAP
items: States carry major service-delivery responsibilities.
Union controls important elastic revenues.
Transfers mediate vertical imbalance.

groups.heading: TRANSFER ARCHITECTURE
items: Finance Commission recommends devolution and grants.
The 2026-31 award retains 41% vertical share.
Horizontal criteria balance equity, need and performance.

groups.heading: GST AND FRICTION
items: GST pools Union-State tax sovereignty.
Council recommendations are not binding.
Cesses, scheme conditions and rate autonomy generate contestation.

stages.answer_line: Transfers are therefore not charity; they are a structural feature of the constitutional division of revenue and responsibility.

stages.title: REPRESENTATION, GOVERNORS, CBI AND CURRENT FRICTION

groups.heading: REPRESENTATION
items: Rajya Sabha carries State voice with unequal representation.
Delimitation changes popular and federal weight.
The defeated 850-seat proposal is not law.

groups.heading: GOVERNOR ASSENT
items: No fixed judicial timeline or deemed assent under current advisory control.
Prolonged unexplained inaction may attract a direction to act.
Court cannot dictate the ultimate constitutional choice.

groups.heading: CBI AND DISPUTE
items: Section 6 consent protects police autonomy.
Constitutional courts may order CBI investigation.
The 2024 West Bengal ruling decided maintainability, not all merits.

stages.answer_line: Population control creates a federal fairness dilemma: equal vote value points toward updated population, while rewarding demographic performance points toward protecting relative representation of lower-growth States.

stages.title: FINAL SYNTHESIS: TRAPS, PYQS AND ANSWER SPINE

groups.heading: PRELIMS CONTROL
items: Union of States does not make States departments.
Residuary power is parliamentary; Article 254 is Concurrent-specific.
GST Council is recommendatory; local bodies are not co-equal sovereigns.

groups.heading: PYQ ROUTES
items: 2020, 2021 and 2022 GS-II questions.
2021 and 2023 Prelims questions.
Objective keys remain inferred where official keys are absent.

groups.heading: MAINS LADDER
items: Define holding-together federalism.
Map federal and centralising features.
Explain distribution, institutions and fiscal capacity.
Use cases and current friction; propose cooperative reform.
